chunks.text:
On Sunday 18 October 2026 Abhijit was Guest of Honour at TKIET (Autonomous), Warananagar, his alma mater, and delivered a 7-hour session titled "Applied Generative AI: Concepts, Architectures and Real-World Implementation" for the Future Ready Engineers Program 2026-27.
Six parts: (1) basics: AI predicts, Gen AI creates, Agentic AI acts; (2) LLMs: tokens, embeddings, the Transformer, LoRA fine-tuning and measuring output quality; (3) prompt engineering: zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, structured output; (4) RAG with a live demo: chunking, hybrid search, reranking, RAGAS evaluation; (5) agentic AI with a live demo: ReAct loops, tools, MCP, agentic RAG with LangGraph; (6) shipping it: latency, cost, reliability.
His key slide: a step that works 95% of the time sounds great, but chain 10 of them and an agent succeeds only about 60% of the time. A demo needs to work once; a product needs to work every time.
All 9+ lab notebooks from the session are open source. The post reached about 1,561 impressions. He thanked the CSE department organisers and acknowledged inspiration from Anant Agarwal's open-source generative AI repository.

chunks.title: LinkedIn > LinkedIn post: "Everyone said Pinecone. I did the math." (week 60)
chunks.text: He needed similarity search over 10,000 face images using ArcFace embeddings (SCRFD detection, crop, ArcFace ResNet50, L2 normalisation). The maths: 10,000 vectors x 512 dimensions x 4 bytes is about 20 MB of RAM, and a query is a single matrix multiply (embeddings @ query_vec) taking about 0.2 ms in-process with numpy. A managed vector database adds 50-200 ms network round-trip, and local ones add 1-5 ms, so he skipped a vector database entirely. His principle: ask "do I need a vector database at all?" and do the math first; vector databases are for millions of vectors, metadata filtering and multi-tenancy.

Head-to-Head (1v1 Duel) - Select any two strategies to compete - Adjust number of rounds (10-200) - View detailed round-by-round history - See visual representation with emojis (🟩 = Cooperate, 🟥 = Defect) 2. Evolutionary Simulation - Population-based natural selection model - Each generation: tournament → elimination → reproduction - Real-time area chart visualization - Adjustable simulation speed - Watch strategies rise and fall over time Strategy Library All strategies are implemented according to game theory literature: - Always Cooperate : Always plays C - Always Defect : Always plays D - Random : 50/50 chance of C or D - Tit For Tat : Starts with C, then copies opponent's last move - Friedman (Grudger) : Cooperates until opponent defects, then defects forever - Joss (Sneaky Tit For Tat) : Like Tit For Tat, but 10% chance to randomly defect - Tit For Two Tats : Only defects if opponent defected in both of the last two rounds - Detective : Plays [C, D, C, C], then: - If opponent ever defected → acts like Tit For Tat - If opponent never defected → acts like Always Defect (exploits the "sucker") Payoff Matrix Tech Stack - Framework : Next.js 14+ (App Router) - Language : TypeScript - Styling : Tailwind CSS - UI Components : shadcn/ui (Radix UI primitives) - Charts : Recharts - Icons : Lucide React Project Structure Getting Started Ins

chunks.title: Portfolio project: ML Model Comparator
chunks.text:
Project "ML Model Comparator". A universal Streamlit app that trains and compares six machine learning models on any CSV dataset, entirely in the browser. Upload data, pick a task and target, and get side-by-side metrics and visualisations with no pre-training. Built for the PGP in AI & DS program at Jio Institute and validated on the UCI Bank Marketing dataset.
Tech: python, streamlit, scikit-learn, xgboost.
Features: Upload any CSV, preview its shape and column types, and auto-detect binary, multiclass or regression tasks. Trains 6 models on the fly with an 80/20 split: Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, KNN, Naive Bayes, Random Forest and XGBoost. One highlighted comparison table with the best value per metric (Accuracy, AUC, Precision, Recall, F1, MCC). Drill-down per model with confusion matrix, radar chart, bar chart and classification report. Automatic preprocessing: label encoding for categoricals and median fill for missing numerics.
Live demo: https://ml-benchmark-app.streamlit.app/

chunks.title: Portfolio project: Energy Demand & Solar Forecasting
chunks.text:
Project "Energy Demand & Solar Forecasting". A time series analysis project that forecasts Italy's 2016 electricity demand and solar power generation, supporting grid stability and renewable energy planning. Built as a team project for the Time Series Analysis course.
Tech: python, statsmodels, prophet, jupyter.
Features: Preprocessing of hourly demand and solar records, with missing value and outlier handling. Exploratory analysis of daily, weekly and yearly seasonality and the demand/solar relationship. Trend, seasonality and residual decomposition, plus ADF stationarity tests and differencing. Forecasting with ARIMA, SARIMA, Holt-Winters and Facebook Prophet, evaluated with RMSE, MAPE and MAE. Forecast plots with confidence intervals and a model comparison report.

chunks.title: Portfolio project: Dementia Care Assistant
chunks.text:
Project "Dementia Care Assistant". A local-first, voice-based cognitive assessment agent for dementia care. A state-machine conversation engine runs memory, orientation, attention and planning tasks and scores them automatically, using locally hosted XTTS v2 for multilingual voice cloning.
Tech: python, flask, xtts-v2, gemini-asr.
Features: Voice cloning with XTTS v2 so the assistant can speak in a familiar voice, all running locally. Cognitive test flow: greeting, three-word memory test, intervening questions, delayed recall and summary. Automated domain-wise scoring from Excellent to Needs Attention. Simple HTML/JS front end with microphone recording and playback. Local-first by design, with Docker Compose for the Flask and XTTS services.

chunks.title: Portfolio project: Ask My PDF
chunks.text:
Project "Ask My PDF". A Next.js app that lets you upload a PDF and chat with it. It extracts and chunks the text, embeds it with OpenAI, retrieves the most relevant passages by cosine similarity and answers with GPT, with voice input for questions.
Tech: nextjs, typescript, openai, rag.
Features: PDF upload with automatic text extraction and chunking (about 500 words with overlap). Retrieval-augmented answers: embeddings plus cosine similarity pick the top matching chunks. Chat with message history and real-time responses. Speech-to-text question input using the Web Speech API. Responsive interface, ready to deploy on Vercel.

chunks.title: Portfolio project: Pathfinder Visualizer

Tech: javascript, html, css, algorithms.
Features: Side-by-side exploration of A* and Dijkstra's algorithm with step-by-step animation. Interactive maze builder: place start and end points and draw obstacles with the mouse. Colour-coded open set, closed set and final path for easy reading. Responsive layout with a one-click grid reset.

chunks.title: Portfolio project: CineMatch
chunks.text:
Project "CineMatch". A personalised movie recommendation app built with Streamlit. Pick a favourite film and it returns five similar titles using TF-IDF vectorisation and cosine similarity, with live posters pulled from the TMDB API.
Tech: python, streamlit, scikit-learn, tmdb-api.
Features: Recommends 5 similar movies for any selected title. Content-based filtering with TF-IDF and cosine similarity on the TMDB movie metadata dataset. Fetches real-time movie posters from the TMDB API. Simple Streamlit interface with precomputed similarity data for fast responses.

chunks.title: Portfolio project: FinanceMe DevOps Pipeline

Tech: aws, terraform, jenkins, docker, ansible.
Features: Terraform provisions four AWS EC2 servers: Jenkins master, build, production and monitoring. Jenkins CI/CD pipeline with a build slave that builds the app and Docker image and pushes to DockerHub. Ansible deploys the Docker container to the production server. Prometheus, Node Exporter and Grafana give continuous monitoring of the build and production servers.
